parts.text:
27 Progressive sound waves of wavelength 20 cm enter the air columns in a closed pipe P and an
open pipe Q. The lengths of the pipes are shown.
P
Q
35 cm
50 cm
In which pipe or pipes are stationary waves formed?
A
P and Q
B
P only
C
Q only
D
neither P nor Q

hints: Notice P is closed at one end and open at the other with length $35\text{ cm}$, while Q is open at both ends with length $50\text{ cm}$, and the driving wavelength is $20\text{ cm}$.

Recall the end conditions: a closed pipe needs a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end, giving $L = (2n-1)\lambda/4$, while an open pipe needs antinodes at both ends, giving $L = n\lambda/2$.

Compare each length with $\lambda/4 = 5\text{ cm}$ and $\lambda/2 = 10\text{ cm}$ to test whether $35\text{ cm}$ is an odd multiple of $5\text{ cm}$ and whether $50\text{ cm}$ is an integer multiple of $10\text{ cm}$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: wavelength $\lambda = 20\text{ cm}$, closed pipe P has $L_P = 35\text{ cm}$, open pipe Q has $L_Q = 50\text{ cm}$.
For closed pipe P, stationary waves require $L_P = (2n-1)\lambda/4$. Here $\lambda/4 = 5\text{ cm}$, so allowed lengths are $5\text{ cm}, 15\text{ cm}, 25\text{ cm}, 35\text{ cm}$ and so on.
Check P: $L_P/ (\lambda/4) = 35/5 = 7$, which is odd, so $2n-1 = 7$. P supports a stationary wave.
For open pipe Q, stationary waves require $L_Q = n\lambda/2$. Here $\lambda/2 = 10\text{ cm}$, so allowed lengths are $10\text{ cm}, 20\text{ cm}, 30\text{ cm}, 40\text{ cm}, 50\text{ cm}$ and so on.
Check Q: $L_Q/(\lambda/2) = 50/10 = 5$, which is an integer, so $n = 5$. Q supports a stationary wave.
Since a stationary wave is formed in both P and Q, This is option A.

A.explanation: Both lengths fit an allowed harmonic for $\lambda = 20\text{ cm}$, so resonance and a stationary wave occur in P and in Q.

B.explanation: P does resonate, but Q also satisfies its resonance condition with length $50\text{ cm}$, so Q cannot be excluded.

C.explanation: Q does resonate, but P also satisfies its resonance condition with length $35\text{ cm}$, so P cannot be excluded.

D.explanation: Both pipes match a stationary wave pattern for this wavelength, so it is wrong to say neither resonates.
